name: Hastings
intro: Hastings sits on the Western Port side of the Peninsula, with a working harbour, mangrove-fringed foreshore and a pier for a slow waterfront walk. It is a practical town rather than a polished resort. Come for the Western Port outlook and a stop on the way south; check current local seafood sellers before making seafood the reason for a special trip. The ferry to French Island and Phillip Island boards at Stony Point, a separate trip south of Hastings, not at Hastings Pier.
factualLede: Hastings is a port town on the Mornington Peninsula's Western Port shoreline, about 75 km from Melbourne, with a public pier, foreshore and working commercial harbour.

heroImage.alt: Hastings pier and fishing fleet looking across Western Port

tldr: Hastings is a working Western Port town with a foreshore, commercial harbour and public pier. The French Island and Phillip Island ferry boards at Stony Point in Crib Point, not at Hastings Pier.
Best for: a Western Port foreshore walk, a pier stop and travellers planning a separate connection from Stony Point.
Allow a few hours; check current seafood trading and ferry times before setting out.
bestSeason: milder days for a Western Port foreshore walk
signature: A working Western Port town with a pier and wide foreshore outlook.
skip: Assuming the Phillip Island ferry leaves from Hastings Pier; the operator lists Stony Point as its mainland terminal.
bestDay: Walk the Hastings foreshore and pier, check current seafood trading before buying lunch, then drive separately to Stony Point only if your onward ferry is booked.
insiderNote: Peninsula Fresh Seafood lists a weather-dependent Friday Hastings Foreshore truck. Check its current location and trading before travelling for seafood.
